title: Mixer Tricks
intro: The Mixer is where a collection of good parts becomes a record. These are the organisational and workflow tricks — the ones that stop a 60‑track session from becoming unmanageable.

tips.t: X shows and hides the Mixer
tips.d: Press X (View > Show Mixer) to show and hide the Mixer in the main window, so you can flip between arrangement and mixer with one key. If you want the Mixer in its own window instead, press Command-2 (Window > Open Mixer).

src.label: Apple — Key commands for Global Commands in Logic Pro for Mac
Apple — Overview of mixing in Logic Pro for Mac

tips.t: ⌥-click a fader to reset it to 0 dB
tips.d: Option-click a channel strip's Volume fader to snap it back to 0 dB. It's the fastest way to undo a level you've talked yourself into.

src.label: Apple — Set channel strip volume in Logic Pro for Mac

tips.d: Option-clicking an unsoloed channel strip solos it and unsolos every other channel strip — one gesture to hear one thing. Option-clicking any active Solo button clears all solos at once. Mute has its own bulk gesture, using Command rather than Option: Command-click a Mute button and every Mute button currently in the same state flips with it, including the output and master strips.

src.label: Apple — Mute and solo channel strips in Logic Pro for Mac

tips.t: Use VCA faders for level groups without changing routing
tips.d: A VCA changes the volume of each channel assigned to it without routing their audio through an aux, so nothing gets re-patched. One consequence: with post-fader sends, what each member sends to an effect follows the VCA, so pulling the VCA down pulls its reverb and delay sends down too, keeping the dry/wet balance. Use Pre Fader sends for anything that must stay constant.

tips.t: Use Summing Stacks for processing groups
tips.d: Select tracks and hit ⇧⌘D, then choose Summing Stack in the dialog that appears. Everything routes to one aux you can compress and EQ as a unit.

tips.t: Create a send and Logic makes the aux for you
tips.d: Click a channel's Send slot and choose a bus. Logic creates the aux channel strip automatically, with that bus already set as its input — unless the bus is already in use as an input on another channel strip.

src.label: Apple — Send signals to multiple destinations in Logic Pro for Mac
Apple — Overview of aux channel strips in Logic Pro (Logic Pro 10.7 guide)

tips.t: Set sends to pre‑fader for headphone mixes and effects that must stay constant
tips.d: Every send has three signal-flow modes, set from the send's pop-up menu: Post Pan (after fader and pan), Post Fader (follows volume but not pan) and Pre Fader (affected by neither). Use a post mode for reverb, so the effect tracks the part. Use Pre Fader for a headphone cue mix, or any send that must stay put while you ride the fader.

tips.t: Colour your tracks and the mixer follows
tips.d: Mixer channels take the track colour. A consistent colour scheme means you find the vocal bus without reading a single label.

src.label: Apple — Change track colors in Logic Pro (Logic Pro 10.7 guide)

tips.t: Bypass with ⌥-click, browse with the slot arrows
tips.d: ⌥-click an insert slot to bypass the plugin without opening it. To browse plugins, click the arrows at the right edge of the slot.

src.label: Apple — Add, remove, move and copy plug-ins in Logic Pro for Mac

tips.t: Drag plugins between insert slots and between channels
tips.d: Reorder your chain by dragging a plug-in up or down, or drag it to another channel strip to move it there. Hold ⌥ and drag it to an unused slot to copy rather than move.
